gen_risks.description: Geopolitical volatility and regional economic shocks in the MENA region could depress venture capital activity and discourage private investor participation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify fund commitments across multiple technology verticals and leverage strategic co-investment partnerships with international DFIs to de-risk private capital.
gen_risks.evidence: Jordan’s small, open economy continues to face vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region.

gen_risks.description: High turnover of core technical and investment staff at the PMU could impair project implementation capacity and delay capital deployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Retain existing qualified ISSF staff by offering competitive market-rate compensation structures and institutionalizing core operational processes.
gen_risks.evidence: In the initial years of operation, ISSF faced challenges linked to, for example, high turnover of the team.

gen_risks.description: Expiration of ISSF's current corporate charter in 2029 creates a legal mismatch with standard 10–12 year VC return horizons.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update ISSF's Articles of Association prior to project effectiveness to convert ISSF into an open-ended private shareholding company.
gen_risks.evidence: return on investment usually takes 10-12 years after capital deployment, whereas currently the ISSF Private Shareholding Company ‘ends’ in 2029.

gen_risks.description: High-growth Jordanian startups may relocate their HQs to GCC countries seeking expansion capital, potentially diluting local economic impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce Side Letter legal covenants requiring beneficiary funds to invest equivalent capital into startups maintaining primary operations and staff in Jordan.
gen_risks.evidence: Availability of long-term funding and market size in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries... prompt high-growth Jordanian startups to expand elsewhere

gen_risks.description: Global and regional venture capital downturns could hamper the project's ability to mobilize $150 million in target private capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Co-invest alongside institutional lead investors and DFIs like IFC, and utilize matching Fund of Funds equity structures to crowd in private investors.
gen_risks.evidence: Despite the global downturn in VC returns in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic...

gen_risks.description: Excessive exposure of project resources to a single VC fund or individual startup could lead to disproportionate capital loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict investment caps in the Project Operations Manual, limiting exposure to any single fund to 15% of loan size and direct co-investments to $500,000.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate and manage concentration risks, the current ISSF Investment Strategy sets out the limit on ISSF investment in one VC fund.

gen_risks.description: Underlying VC fund managers could engage in fraud, mismanagement, or regulatory non-compliance, leading to financial loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate comprehensive Legal, Corporate, and Operational Due Diligence (ODD) prior to capital commitment and maintain continuous ODD oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure that underlying funds follow robust operational practices and have the tools and capacity to monitor risks such as fraud, mismanagement, or regulatory non-compliance.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate PMU capacity regarding World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) could cause compliance delays or risk mismanagement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified E&S officer to the PMU and establish an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) after effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: ISSF requires improved E&S risks and impacts management capacity, especially in the implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESS).

gen_risks.description: Improper e-waste disposal by beneficiary tech SMEs could result in environmental pollution and public health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate mandatory E&S screening criteria into sub-venture application processes and mandate good e-waste recycling practices in fund legal documents.
gen_risks.evidence: SMEs’ supported activities may cause environmental impacts connected to mismanagement of e-waste, including pollution, Occupational Health and Safety...

gen_risks.description: Workers in beneficiary ICT startups may face workplace discrimination, poor employment conditions, or sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement ESCP gap-filling measures on labor rights, enforce workplace codes of conduct, and establish confidential SEA/SH-sensitive grievance mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Additional labor risks related to ICT start-ups include terms and conditions of employment, discrimination, and sexual harassment...

gen_risks.description: Tech startups supported by the fund could encounter data privacy breaches, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, or exacerbate the digital divide.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish data privacy guidelines and social risk screening checklists within the ESMS for financial intermediaries and target tech ventures.
gen_risks.evidence: the proposed Project could entail social risks, including poor labor and working conditions, limited stakeholder engagement, the digital divide, data privacy and security risks

gen_risks.description: Women and youth entrepreneurs may face persistent social or structural barriers preventing equal participation in equity funding.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a Gender Action Plan with targeted outreach, enforce a 30% target for female-owned/led beneficiaries, and mandate female representation on the ISSF Board/IC.
gen_risks.evidence: there is a risk that they may not fully benefit if specific barriers to their participation are not effectively addressed.

gen_risks.description: Gaps in Jordanian national labor law regarding non-discrimination, worker organizations, and supply chain oversight may conflict with World Bank ESS2.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt specific gap-filling measures set forth in the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) to ensure full compliance with ESS2 standards.
gen_risks.evidence: There are gaps with ESS2 in the following areas: lack of non-discrimination provisions based on gender, disability and citizenship; worker’s organizations

gen_risks.description: Prolonged investment approval processes and governance reviews could delay capital allocation to beneficiary VC funds and startups.
gen_risks.mitigation: Streamline governance by separating Board oversight from Investment Committee management and conduct biannual beneficiary surveys to optimize turnaround times.
gen_risks.evidence: when it comes to the duration of the investment review/approval processes.

gen_risks.description: Climate change hazards such as severe droughts and extreme weather events could disrupt startup supply chains and physical business operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply Paris Alignment screening criteria to project investments and allocate 10% of total capital toward greentech and climate-resilient solutions.
gen_risks.evidence: expected decrease in total precipitation, with increased variability in the location, timing, and quantity of rainfall; increased drought occurrence, and more frequent extreme events.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. External economic shocks, regional instability and related uncertainties, or a downturn in global venture capital markets could reduce investor confidence and slow private capital mobilization. Additionally, Jordan's nascent venture capital market and competition from more developed ecosystems in neighboring countries may impact startup retention and funding.

Other risks are rated Substantial and relate to geopolitical risk. Jordan's strategic location makes it susceptible to a complex set of geopolitical challenges that have intensified in recent years, due to the current Conflict in the Middle East and its repercussions for investment, trade, and tourism in the region. Increasing geopolitical risks may prompt adjustments in policy and budgetary priorities and/or contribute to delays in implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: By combining regional and global diplomacy, building international partnerships, staying the course on political and economic modernization reforms, implementing prudent fiscal policies, and strategic security measures, Jordan has maintained its resilience and stability despite continuous crises.
